title.narrative: Grant for Capacity Building of the Finance Department of the Government of Uttar Pradesh

description.narrative: As part of the Country Assistance Strategy (CAS), the World Bank helped four focus states, including UP, to conduct State Financial Accountability Assessment (SFAA) studies. The UP SFAA report identified poor cash, debt and guarantee management, a weak monitoring and control environment and overly complex regulatory framework as major weaknesses of the financial management system in the state. The analysis suggested that there was significant scope for the Government of Uttar Pradesh (GoUP) to improve efficiency and effectiveness of public spending through further consolidation of budget, better matching of accountability with responsibility, robust enforcement of accountability and greater transparency. Therefore, to help GoUP to pilot reforms in some areas identified by the SFAA and to enable them to build on their own ongoing fiscal reform program, IDF funding is sought. The proposed IDF will support pilots in the following areas four focus areas: (a) cash, debt and guarantee management, (b) building capacity of the state's financial management training institute (FMRTI), (c) simplification and revision of the state's financial rules and procedures and (d) development of MTEF methodology for departmental budgeting and running a pilot MTEF in one major spending departments. The focus areas have been identified by GoUP because if the pilots undertaken here are successful, they will provide the Ministry of Finance will a strong lever to engage in a widespread budgetary reform program. In addition to this, the choice of a small pilot driven program is predicated on the unstable political environment in the state, as incremental pilots will be easier to undertake, sustain and build upon rather than a widespread program. So, the IDF is being designed such that its funds and interventions supplement GoUP's own funds and initiatives in the identified areas and the pilot reform program in the four focus areas identified for support by the grant will be led, owned and managed by GoUP's own staff from the Ministry of Finance with consultant input and support being financed by the grant. GoUP's ownership and support of the pilot reforms will be demonstrated by the fact that the grant agreement will have a Legal covenant that the Secretary-Finance and the Deputy Secretary-Finance (Budget) who led the SFAA and the IDF preparation from GoUP should be in place throughout the period of the grant to Task Lead the grant from GoUP side. To enhance capacities of the key institutions under the Finance Department to improve financial management, reduce fiduciary risks and achieve the Government's overall development objective. The specific objectives are to (i) strengthen debt, guarantee and cash management systems in GoUP (ii) Build capacity of the Financial Management and Training Research Institute of Uttar Pradesh (iii) Pilot a MTEF in one select department (iv) Simplify and improve financial rules and procedures in GoUP
